items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: he played a chorus, I played a chorus on trumpet... Harry Edison.

ctx.x: Yes, he played a chorus, I played a chorus on trumpet, Clark Terry, Claude Perry, Dizzy Gillespie, John Faddis, and ... is that 6? Dizzy Gillespie, Claude Perry, Clark Terry, Doc Cheatham, Faddis, Carter -- Faddis, Carter -- who was the other one? There was another one -- there were 6 of us. Harry Edison.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: we took ... Harry Sweets Edison as our star trumpet player.

ctx.x: To ask you if you have an overall impression of that, I'm afraid may not be a very meaningful question. But let's leave it as asked. Before we do that, tell us who you took along with you.
Well, we took Gildo Mahoney, on the piano, John B. Williams on the bass, Earl Palmer on the drums, and Harry Sweets Edison as our star trumpet player.

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Like the late great Ben Webster, Don Byas, Stuff Smith, Rex Stewart, Benny Carter lived in Europe for years.

ctx.x: It’s been a great gift of our country to the world.

Oh, yes, to the world. He was, he played, I don’t think he missed any place on this earth playing. He played just about every place, and played for royalty, they appreciated him over there very much. In fact the Europeans appreciate jazz music more than Americans, although it’s an American art form. But it’s appreciated more in Europe. And as you know, a lot of the musicians have migrated to Europe because they appreciate them more then they do here in America. Like the late great Ben Webster, Don Byas, Stuff…

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I know I would’ve had to give an account of myself to your very good friend, Benny Carter

ctx.x: Just for the record it is now August the 20th. It’s Friday and I have the great pleasure of sitting with Harry “Sweets” Edison in Los Angeles beginning our oral history interview for the Smithsonian. And “Sweets,” we appreciate your taking this time.

Well, you know you’re one of my favorite people, Ed, and I couldn’t wait to get back from Europe because I knew we had made this appointment for today. I hurried up and got here because I didn’t want to disappoint you and I know I would’ve had to give an account of myself to your very good friend, Benny Carter (laughs).

Well, by tomorrow you may be rushing back to Europe after a couple hours of this (both laugh) but anyway, I just want to start before we go back into the chronology of your illustrious career. I want to start with a more recent event. Did the City of Los Angeles honor you?
